title: Complexity concentration as a god-class and god-method detector: a pre-registered test of a scale-free outlier rule against tool definitions and human labels
abstract: arXiv:2610.32466v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: God-class and god-method detectors mark concentrated complexity with a raw-scale threshold, a constant fitted on a corpus and re-fitted when the population moves. This paper pre-registers a test of a rule with no raw-scale constant: a unit is a god unit when its complexity is a robust outlier for its own codebase, a modified z-score of 3.5 or more. On 445 repositories in ten languages, 171 of them Java, and the 492 Java repositories of MLCQ, the rule is scored against PMD's GodClass, MLCQ's reviewers and two further definitions, with signal and cutoff chosen on half the repositories and read on the rest. LLM-written code may gather its complexity differently, the case for a detector that needs no re-fitting; the first question is whether one can match the scale of existing human-written code. The verdict is inconclusive on both populations, by different arms. The rule ranks PMD's god classes from the per-file maximum of cognitive complex

translated_title: 复杂度集中作为上帝类与上帝方法检测器：一项针对无标度离群点规则与工具定义及人工标注对比的预注册检验
translated_abstract: 上帝类和上帝方法检测器用原始尺度的阈值来标记集中的复杂度，而该阈值是在语料库上拟合出的常数，当总体（代码库分布）发生变化时就需要重新拟合。本文对一条不依赖原始尺度常数的规则进行了预注册检验：当一个单元的复杂度相对其自身代码库而言是稳健的离群点（修正z分数达到3.5或以上）时，该单元即被判定为“上帝单元”。在涵盖十种语言、其中171个为Java的445个代码库，以及MLCQ数据集中492个Java代码库上，该规则与PMD的GodClass定义、MLCQ的人工评审者标注以及其他两种定义进行了对比评分，信号指标与截断值在一半代码库上选取，并在其余代码库上验证。LLM编写的代码可能以不同方式聚集其复杂度，这正需要一个无需重新拟合的检测器；而首要问题是：该规则能否在规模上匹配现有由人类编写的代码。最终结论在两个人群上均不确定，且各自通过不同的检验分支得出。该规则从每文件认知复杂度的最大值出发，对PMD识别出的上帝类进行排序。
tldr: 本文预注册检验了一种不依赖原始尺度阈值的上帝类/上帝方法检测新规则——即当单元复杂度在其自身代码库中构成稳健离群点（修正z分数≥3.5）时判定为“上帝单元”，但在445个多语言代码库与492个Java代码库上与PMD及MLCQ等现有定义对比后，结论尚不确定。
en_tdlr: This paper pre-registered a test of a scale-free god-class/god-method detection rule that flags units whose complexity is a robust outlier (modified z-score ≥ 3.5) within their own codebase, but the verdict was inconclusive when scored against PMD's GodClass, MLCQ's human labels, and other definitions across 445 multilingual and 492 Java repositories.
